title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review round 6 findings on PR #524 head 8dfbd25
description:
Supervisor self-review round 6 of PR #524 head 8dfbd25. FIVE findings: one HIGH, two MEDIUM, two LOW. The sweep independently re-verified as correct the half-open interval arithmetic (including the pending-successor case), __future__ sort-before-real semantics, resolveCampaignPosition savepoint nesting and failed-turn chronology, parseCampaignPosition round-trip canonicality, the seenRuleIdentities/includeAllActive interaction, and automatic checkpoint/migration pickup.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev9 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev9, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 8dfbd25. npm ci already run.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (HIGH) — an ambiguity ruling can never be superseded. Introduced by the very first review fix on this PR.
=============================================================
supersedeCampaignRule validates the ALREADY-PERSISTED prior rule against the SUCCESSOR's validation options:
    validateCampaignRule(prior, input.validation);
    validateCampaignRules([{ ...prior, status: 'superseded', ... }, successor], input.validation);
validateCampaignRule on a ruling with ambiguity provenance calls ambiguityFor(ambiguityId, options) and fails with 'unknown ambiguity ...' when it does not resolve. A caller replacing ruling R (ambiguity X) with a house rule, or with a ruling for a DIFFERENT ambiguity Y, naturally supplies validation describing only the successor — so the call throws on the prior, which was already validated at creation and is not being changed semantically.
REPRODUCED at 8dfbd25 (supervisor): create a ruling for ambiguity:x, then supersede it with a plain house rule ->
    CampaignRuleError: unknown ambiguity ambiguity:x
This blocks the ambiguity-ruling lifecycle outright, which eshyra-jhpt.6 and .7 are built on. Existing store tests only supersede rules that share the successor's provenance, so the path is untested.
PROVENANCE OF THE DEFECT: `validateCampaignRule(prior, input.validation)` was added by the first blocking-review fix (eshyra-jhpt.2.4) at the supervisor's instruction, to stop validation being fed a prior whose status had been rewritten. That instruction was right about the status and wrong about the options: the prior must be checked for the invariants supersession actually changes, not re-validated as if it were being created now.
FIX: validate the prior only for what supersession changes — identity, campaign, status/supersededBy transition — and do not re-run provenance/ambiguity validation against the successor's options. If you believe the prior's ambiguity linkage must still be checked, resolve it from the pack via ambiguityLookup rather than from the caller's successor-scoped options, and say why. Keep the round-1 property intact: the prior's REAL stored status must still be what gets checked, never a rewritten copy.
EVIDENCE: supersede an ambiguity ruling with (a) a house rule, (b) a ruling for a different ambiguity, and (c) a ruling for the same ambiguity — all succeed with correct chain state; and the round-1 guards (already-superseded, revoked prior) still reject.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 (MEDIUM) — the recoverable category was drawn too wide: packaging defects now degrade silently.
=============================================================
Round 5 asked for a positive category so pack-CONTENT failures degrade by construction. The implementation marks the BASE RulesPackError constructor (rules/types.ts) plus CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError, so every RulesPackError in the codebase is now recoverable. That includes packaging defects: a campaign still bound to the retired 'rules:dnd5e-srd' placeholder, or a shipped build with a corrupt or missing data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/. bundledSrdPack.ts documents exactly that case as "a packaging defect, not a recoverable runtime condition", yet the turn now proceeds with an AMBIGUITY SOURCE UNAVAILABLE line, all ambiguity metadata dropped, and every active ambiguity ruling flattened into the generic rules list — while tools later fail on the same binding with a different error. The operator sees degraded play instead of a clear failure.
This is partly the supervisor's fault: round 5 said "pack content" and the marker was applied to the whole error base class. The category is right; its membership is wrong.
FIX: mark only the errors that represent unusable pack CONTENT encountered while interpreting a resolved pack — CampaignRulesPackAuthoringError and the ambiguity-interpretation failures — not the base RulesPackError and not binding/packaging resolution failures. Keep it a positive category (a future content-error class opts in by marking itself); just narrow the membership. Then confirm the round-3 finding-1 behaviour is preserved for the case it was actually about, and state explicitly which failures now degrade and which are fatal.

=============================================================
FINDING 3 (MEDIUM) — the ambiguity boundary's try wraps far more than the comment claims.
=============================================================
campaignContext.ts ambiguitiesFromStack wraps the WHOLE record loop, not just the optRulesAmbiguities call, and rethrows anything unmarked as CampaignRulesPackAuthoringError. So a genuine programming error — a TypeError from iterating stack.recordsByKey after some future stack-resolution change — becomes a marked recoverable error, is swallowed by finding 2's handler, and surfaces only as a prompt line reading "AMBIGUITY SOURCE UNAVAILABLE: Cannot read properties of undefined". The comment says "unrelated failures retain their original behavior outside this boundary"; the boundary is wider than the comment describes.
FIX: narrow the try to the optRulesAmbiguities call itself, so only pack-content interpretation is reclassified. Test that a non-pack error thrown from the surrounding loop propagates unchanged.

=============================================================
FINDING 4 (LOW) — revokeCampaignRule is the only mutation whose guards and write are not in one transaction.
=============================================================
createCampaignRule and supersedeCampaignRule wrap their writes in withTransaction; revokeCampaignRule runs assertCurrentPosition, getCampaignRule, the position/ordering guards and the UPDATE directly on db. If another writer advances campaign_turn_position between the check and the update, the revocation commits against a position that is no longer current — precisely what those guards exist to prevent.
FIX: wrap it in withTransaction like its siblings. Note also that supersedeCampaignRule performs its guard reads before opening its transaction, a smaller version of the same window; close that too if it is cheap.

=============================================================
FINDING 5 (LOW, performance) — the per-turn path scans the campaign's whole rule history twice.
=============================================================
assembleCampaignRulesContext calls activeRows twice per turn, each call decoding and projecting every revoked and superseded row in the campaign's history.
FIX: compute the active row set once per assembly and share it between the two lists. Behaviour must not change.
Index note: activeRows does every position predicate in JS, so the two position indexes from migration 0025 can never be chosen. That is already tracked as eshyra-jhpt.2.5 — do NOT change indexes or migrations here. If you judge that an `effective_position <= ?` prefilter on the encoded string is a safe superset given the cp1~<12-digit ordinal>~ layout, record the reasoning on eshyra-jhpt.2.5 rather than implementing it in this PR.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against 8dfbd25; report observed counts and quote asserted guard messages.
  - Every negative assertion must assert the distinctive guard message.
  - Do not weaken existing tests, do not touch merged migrations, the position encoding, eshyra-umyb, eshyra-jhpt.2.5, or eshyra-l30k.
  - Preserve every earlier fix, in particular: the prior rule's real stored status is what gets validated (round 1), deterministic future-anchor ordering (round 4), and returning exactly what was persisted (round 5).

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution.
